title: A handoff request that never names a skill is the unnamed twin of explicit-name@2
prompt: 把当前任务整理成一份交接说明，写到工作区的 HANDOFF.md。

fixture.notes: An empty disposable workspace; the skill body comes from the checkout, not from the fixture.

graders.expects: every read_skill call used name=task-handoff; no other workflow was loaded instead
HANDOFF.md has at least three headings, so it is a document rather than one paragraph

cleanup: Discard the trial workspace; the skill body is packaged with the checkout and is never modified.
notes: Deliberate twin of skill-selection/explicit-name@2: same deliverable, same skill, same authority, and the only difference is that this prompt neither names the skill nor states an order. Run together they answer a question neither can alone — whether the name in the prompt is what produces the read. This case has no ordering grader on purpose: nothing in the prompt asks for an order, so grading one would be the false negative that explicit-name v2 was rewritten to avoid. Content quality stays semantic and unasserted.
